purpose: Read-mode editorial storyboard; original diagrams specified, not rendered assets.

modeContract.switchBehavior: Preserve shared lesson, practice answers, progress and preferences. Switching mode never resets or completes a lesson. Map Watch chapter cues to Read panel IDs; when no precise cue exists, switch at the same lesson and announce that position.
modeContract.fullText: Always expose Full lesson text as semantic HTML, including every original content paragraph, activity, knowledge check and referenced source. Never hide the only accessible equivalent behind animation.
modeContract.practice: Use the identical source activity and knowledgeCheck in both modes. Do not duplicate scoring or alter answer IDs.
modeContract.watchUnavailable: Keep Read accessible. Label Watch unavailable or preparing honestly; never display a fake playable asset.

deliveryNote: Compact derivative. Read original course JSON for verbatim content, activities, checks, source links and assessment keys. All diagrams are specified-not-rendered native HTML/CSS or accessible SVG. No production artwork is claimed. Canonical design artifact is read-storyboards.json.

panelDefaults.interaction: Explicit Next/Back and optional native details; no auto-advance. Keep callouts visible; full source text remains available.
panelDefaults.visualAssetType: original semantic diagram or native case card
panelDefaults.textEquivalent: Use panel copy plus mapped source paragraphs; use original numerical tables where specified.

courses.title: Bloom’s Taxonomy: Match the Learning to the Work

panels.title: Use the revised category names
copy: Remember → Understand → Apply → Analyze → Evaluate → Create
panels.visualSpecification: Six equal-weight labeled task cards in sequence; no pyramid implying people or work are ranked.
panels.callout: This sample uses the 2001 revision. Knowledge also varies: factual, conceptual, procedural, metacognitive.

panels.title: Compare what the learner actually does
copy: Recall urgent-ticket definition: Remember.
Explain urgent versus routine: Understand.
Use a triage rule: Apply.
panels.visualSpecification: Three same-context task cards; signal the action and evidence in each.

panels.title: Choose the needed performance
copy: A routine procedure can appropriately require Apply.
The highest-sounding label is not automatically better.
panels.visualSpecification: Work requirement connected to a category-selection card rather than an upward achievement ladder.

panels.title: Try the decision, then check your reasoning
copy: Choose a response and explain the evidence behind it.
Read the option-specific feedback, then try the knowledge check.
panels.visualSpecification: One original case card above a semantic radio-choice group. Feedback appears directly under the chosen option; knowledge check follows as a separate step in the same panel. No decorative character art needed.
panels.callout: Practice remains available in both Read and Watch. Selected-response success does not establish production mastery.

lessons.title: 2. Classify the task, not just its verb

panels.title: Look beyond the verb
copy: “Identify” can mean recall or analysis.
Inspect content, conditions, references, novelty and reasoning.
panels.visualSpecification: Same verb on two task cards with different evidence requirements.

panels.title: Compare four different tasks
copy: Apply: execute the rule.
Analyze: distinguish shared causes.
Evaluate: judge proposals against criteria.
Create: develop a coherent new plan.
panels.visualSpecification: Four equal task cards, revealed individually with the fictional rule card always available.

panels.title: Name the knowledge and the action
copy: Factual: queue name; conceptual: impact and urgency.
Procedural: how to triage; metacognitive: how to check uncertainty.
The learner must use ___ knowledge to ___.
panels.visualSpecification: Two-axis conceptual matrix, with no numeric scores or ranking of learners.
panels.callout: These dimensions describe tasks, not a learner’s intelligence or worth.

lessons.title: 3. Turn an intention into an observable objective

panels.title: Make the evidence observable
copy: Specify behavior, conditions and standard.
panels.visualSpecification: Three labeled objective components with the corresponding source-example text adjacent.

panels.title: Inspect a complete objective
copy: Given a rule card and four fictional tickets, assign priorities with at least three correct.
panels.visualSpecification: Sentence segmented into Condition, Behavior, Standard using labels and underlines as well as color.
panels.callout: The 3/4 criterion is illustrative, not a validated safety threshold. Use time limits only when job-relevant and fair.

copy: Find the objective, practice and success evidence.
Flag unsupported claims.

copy: Draft A: definitions plus terminology quiz.
Draft B: rule, worked case, supported practice, new-case check and job aid.
panels.visualSpecification: Two original curriculum strips; highlight where B elicits the required rule-use decision.
